items.headline: U.S. Stocks Conclude Record-Setting Week with Broad Gains
items.summary: U.S. stock markets finished a record-setting week on a positive note, with all major indices advancing. Sentiment improved as earlier jitters regarding artificial intelligence (AI) sector performance eased. The rally was broad, though technology stocks saw some mixed performance, while defensive sectors like Real Estate and Energy led gains.

items.headline: Humana Surges on Strong Ratings
items.summary: Humana ($HUM) rallied 11.6% after the insurer reported encouraging data regarding its quality ratings for Medicare Advantage plans, accompanied by an analyst upgrade.

items.headline: Crown Castle Jumps on SpaceX Deal
items.summary: Crown Castle ($CCI) rose 15.60% following news that SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio, fueling optimism for wireless infrastructure demand.

items.headline: Amazon Leads Tech Rebound
items.summary: Amazon.com Inc. ($AMZN) advanced 3.29% to close at $262.43, as software and cloud stocks recovered from concerns earlier in the week regarding OpenAI's revenue outlook.

items.headline: T-Mobile US Slides on Spectrum Deal Impact
items.summary: T-Mobile US ($TMUS) fell 13.27% due to increased competition concerns following SpaceX's agreement to acquire a nationwide spectrum portfolio for Starlink Mobile services.

items.headline: Apple Drops on iPhone Production Cuts
items.summary: Apple Inc. ($AAPL) declined 1.11% to $336.64 after reports suggested the company had reduced component orders for its next iPhone series amid weak demand.

items.headline: Delta Air Lines Falls on Earnings Miss and Guidance Cut
items.summary: Delta Air Lines ($DAL) slipped after reporting Q3 adjusted earnings per share of $1.72, missing the $1.96 consensus, and cutting its full-year EPS forecast to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50.

items.headline: Real Estate and Energy Lead Sector Gains; Tech Lags Amid AI Concerns
items.summary: On Friday, Real Estate was the top-performing sector, gaining 1.88%, fueled by wireless infrastructure companies and residential real estate stocks. Energy also saw significant gains, with the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) up 3%. Conversely, the Technology sector lagged, declining 0.52%, with communication services down 0.4%. Concerns over OpenAI's revenue outlook contributed to a mixed performance for tech, especially AI and semiconductor stocks.

items.headline: Michigan Consumer Sentiment Falls, Inflation Expectations Tick Up
items.summary: The University of Michigan's preliminary October Consumer Sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, reaching its lowest level since May. Year-ahead inflation expectations also ticked up to 4.7% from 4.6%, indicating persistent concerns among consumers.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Rise, Oil Prices Stabilize on Geopolitical Developments
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.24%. Meanwhile, Brent crude prices ticked higher, settling at $104.72 per barrel, up 0.4%, after an early-morning dip. Oil market stability was aided by President Trump's statements ruling out an immediate attack on Iran and an agreement for Russia to release diesel to global markets, easing supply concerns.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season to Accelerate Next Week with Major Banks Reporting
items.summary: Following Delta Air Lines' Q3 earnings report on Friday, which saw the airline miss consensus estimates, the third-quarter earnings season is set to gather momentum next week. Major banks are scheduled to report, shifting the earnings season into higher gear.
